en: This changes the OpenXR projection layer FOV, not the CP2077 camera FOV.

Draw only your hands: the rest of the body and all clothing are hidden,
the arms are cut at the wrists. The tactical belt and the weapons
hanging in their holsters stay visible.

Dumps gizmo vs. bone poses to vrik_diag.txt (next to dxgi.dll)
for tuning the arm IK. Same as the CET 'Log VR Diag' button.

Move the player capsule with physical horizontal head movement.
Uses native collision/steps and preserves stick or WASD movement.
Suspended in menus, vehicles and scripted movement.

Hybrid: use the head cone while upright.
Looking down by 10 degrees or bending by 5 degrees uses HMD + controllers.
Return below 8 / 3 degrees; the current body heading is preserved at handover.
HMD + controllers always disables the body cones. Missing tracking holds heading.

Applies only on foot. VRIK yields to the scene animation at or above this tier.
The vehicle threshold is configured separately below.

Applies in vehicles, including passenger window combat.
VRIK yields to the scene animation at or above this tier. Never keeps VRIK enabled.

While a scene drives the camera, its turning within this angle does not
turn the view; past it the view eases after the scene camera. Cuts still switch at once.
0 = the scene camera exactly as the game moves it. Default: 30 degrees.

How far your head may turn before the body starts coming around.
The body settles toward the centre, then restores the full free-look zone.
Default: 10 degrees. Hybrid uses this value while looking ahead.

Extra room to reach chest-mounted items.
Blends in from 10 to 30 degrees of downward head tilt.
Never narrows the normal cone; set the same value to disable widening.

One fixed cone on the surface and underwater.
Looking down and physical bending do not widen it. Default: 5 degrees.
Body free-look cones are disabled in HMD + controllers mode.
Hybrid: head cone upright; HMD + controllers when looking down or bending.

Small physical head movements leave the body in place.
Outside this zone the body follows smoothly; camera tracking remains immediate.
active cone %.1f deg | realign %+.1f deg | head-vs-body %+.1f deg
Hand IK Calibration (per hand: R = right, L = left)
AUTO-CALIBRATING: stretch arms STRAIGHT OUT to the sides,
stand straight facing forward. Hold for %.1fs (%.0f%%).

Press once, then stretch BOTH gizmo hands OUT to the sides at shoulder height
and stand straight facing forward. The mod measures the visible controller
positions, computes shoulder pivots + arm scale, and saves the result
to vrik_calibration.ini.
Camera: neck + 15 cm forward, eyes + 10 cm up

Uses the neutral neck, 15 cm forward and 10 cm above reference eyes.
Resets camera trims; no stance, head direction or Bake measurement is needed.

The engine hooks did not load, so everything below is inert and the headset is on the plain mono path. Either CyberpunkVR_StereoModuleEnable is 0, or bin\x64\vrport_nostereo.txt exists. See the "Stereo:" line in cyberpunkvrport.log.
No second eye right now -> both eyes get MAIN (mono)
Expected in menus and while loading. If it stays here in gameplay: the VRCAM component is off, or vrcam.json names a camera the player entity does not carry.
Stereo submit off -> both eyes get MAIN (mono)
vrcam eye age %u ms  (stale over %u)   eye submits %llu
vrcam eye: never produced a frame

Off = the old behaviour, MAIN duplicated into both eyes.
On = the %s eye gets the VRCAM view's own final colour --
the same image the desktop mirror shows -- re-encoded to the
swapchain's sRGB format and scaled to the eye size.
snapshot copies %llu   skips %llu   vrcam RTV hits %llu

How long the last VRCAM frame stays usable. Past this the %s
eye falls back to MAIN -- one eye frozen while the other moves
is far worse to look at than mono.
VRCAM DLSS: %s  (follows MAIN's upscaler, no switch)

On whenever MAIN is upscaling with DLSS: vrcam gets its own
Streamline viewport and renders below its target.
Off for DLAA / TAA / no upscaler. Change it in the game's
graphics settings, not here.
Match VRCAM projection to MAIN  (fov / zoom / near / far)
vrcam fov %.2f  (asset %.2f)   main yy %.5f  fov %.2f   ADS x%.3f

A small panel that stays up after F10 is closed, reporting what the ENGINE did to the camera when the sights came up:
delta and peak in centimetres, right/forward/up in the heading's own basis, against a baseline captured while hip firing.
Stereo submission is unaffected.
Normalised position in the eye image
Committed snapshot of the VRCAM final

Off = read the engine's transient directly. That target is a
frame-graph allocation which a later pass aliases, which is what
made the image alternate bright/dark. Leave on.
Snapshot at the tonemap node instead of RenderFinal2D
Grab the wheel with the grips

While DRIVING, bring a hand to where the driving animation holds the
wheel (or the handlebars) and squeeze that grip: the arm is handed back
to the game's own animation -- hand on the wheel, fingers wrapped around
it -- instead of following the controller. Release the grip and it goes
back to your hand.

Each hand is independent: hold the wheel with one and keep the other on
a gun. While a hand is at the wheel that grip does nothing else (no
holster equip, no magazine grab).

How close your hand has to be to the animated hand before the
grip counts as grabbing the wheel. Bigger = easier to catch a
wheel you cannot see; too big and every grip in a car grabs.

Wheel sensitivity: hand rotation from the grab position to full lock.
One hand uses a hub calibrated where you grab; two use their connecting line.
Adding or releasing a hand keeps the current turn.
180 = a half turn to either full lock (default). Lower = more sensitive.
The car's cabin wheel has twice its native travel; road-wheel lock is unchanged.
Travel beyond full lock keeps the same neutral position.

Tilt around centre that steers nothing at all.
Raise it if the car drifts while you hold the wheel straight;
every degree here is a degree of dead wheel off centre.
The full range still ends at 'Full lock at', so widening the
deadzone does not make the steering jump.

Gently anticipate a continuing turn from recent hand movement.
Limited to 8 ms and 0.5 degrees; neutral stays unchanged.
Prediction stops on a pause, reversal or grip change.
Off by default. It cannot anticipate the start of a turn.
Horn -- hand on the wheel hub

While DRIVING, put a hand on the MIDDLE of the wheel -- where you would
slap a real horn -- and the car honks for as long as it stays there.
No grip needed; a hand that is GRABBING the wheel never honks.

How near the wheel centre the hand counts as on the hub.
Bigger = easier to find the horn without seeing it; too big
and it reaches the rim, so every grab honks.
Trigger fires the gun while driving

Draw a weapon in the driver seat and the RIGHT TRIGGER stops being the
throttle and becomes the gun: drive with the left hand on the wheel and
shoot with the right.

The throttle LATCHES at whatever it was when the weapon came out, so the
car keeps rolling, and the LEFT STICK forward/back trims that speed while
you shoot. Holster the weapon and the trigger is the throttle again.

While the weapon is out the left stick's forward/back is taken by the
trim: no lean / rock and no autodrive gesture until you holster.

How much of the throttle's full travel the left stick adds or
removes per second while a weapon is out.
0.5 = two seconds held to go from idle to floored.
driving %d   at wheel  L %d R %d   hold  L %.2f R %.2f
steer  %+.1f deg  ->  stick %+.2f     horn  L %d R %d

Head offsets in GENERAL are a standing calibration. Seated, the game's own
vehicle camera is already where it should be -- which is why the port drops
its two automatic bakes in a vehicle -- so a standing offset carries the view
off the seat instead of correcting it.

These three are added to the Head sliders while you are in a vehicle and
ignored the moment you step out, so the car and the street can be tuned
separately. Zero = the car keeps exactly the offset it has today.
Hold the panel heading inside this yaw range; catch up beyond it.
Real %.1f FPS   Framegen %.1f FPS   Output %.1f FPS
GPU frame timing: waiting for completed queries
Game GPU memory %.2f GiB   Budget %.2f GiB
RAM %.2f / %.2f GiB   Game working set %.2f GiB
CPU: captured frame cadence. GPU: graphics-queue frame interval. Peaks: last 2 seconds.
Output FPS excludes repeated frames; it is not a headset scanout measurement.
Lows use the mean of the slowest 1%% / 0.1%% of real-frame intervals. Hardware polling: 1 Hz.
FPS overlay and statistics are off.
Contrast-adaptive sharpening for both eyes. 0 = off, 1 = full strength. Disabled automatically with game DLAA.
The center follows game DLSS/DLAA. Peripheral DLAA uses 100%% / 75%% / 50%% of the game's render resolution.
Full-quality region width as a percentage of each eye image.
Full-quality region height as a percentage of each eye image.
Percentage of eye-image width. Negative = left, positive = right.
Percentage of eye-image height. Negative = up, positive = down toward the hands.
DLSS GPU: native %.2f ms / foveated %.2f ms
Render sun cascades once for both eyes. Shadow quality and distance remain controlled by the game.
Magnifying scope lenses while the view moves: share of the stabilised image (percent). Higher: no blinking of lights and grates, softer. 0 = off. Standing still the lens is untouched.
Opaque scene materials in both eyes. The center stays 1 x 1. Unsupported 4 x 4 falls back to 2 x 2.
Skips shading the parts of each eye image the lens never shows. The visible area is unchanged.

Size of the shaded area as a percentage of the eye's field of view: 100%% touches its edges, 141%% masks nothing inside it.
Lower it until a dark border appears at the edge of the lens, then raise it until the border is gone.
Locomotion direction is set in the Controls tab.

Suppress mouse/right-stick pitch so only the HMD controls
vertical look. Applied by the CET VRIK mod and the
XInput merge. On by default.

Off by default for a clean cyberpunkvrport.log. Enable only
when capturing ClipCursor / depth / hook diagnostics.
While frame generation is enabled, hand smoothing runs at its rate times xr_hand_lerp_framegen_scale (1.10; 0 turns it off).
DLSS Frame Generation is not available here (%s); FidelityFX is used.
NVIDIA optical flow is not available on this GPU; FidelityFX optical flow is used.

The game's motion vectors already describe almost all motion; optical flow adds GPU time
and memory for what they miss (some particles and effects).
NVIDIA's frame generation model on the game's motion vectors and depth. Highest quality, RTX 40/50.
Up to half headset refresh. Leaves more GPU time for generated frames when adjacent real frames are being missed.
Uses game motion vectors and depth in both eyes. Adds one intermediate frame between real frames.
Catch up beyond the cone, or after 3 seconds at rest when the yaw offset is over 10 degrees inside it.

Off: the HUD has the same direction in both eyes.
On: place it at the selected physical depth.
Used while the loot panel and item description are visible. Default: 10 degrees.
Interaction prompts and dialog choices share this panel. It follows only beyond the cone; no delayed catch-up at rest.
Not currently visible in gameplay; settings are still saved.
Movement, weapon aiming and physical interaction shortcuts.

The two controllers trade roles: the left trigger fires and the right one aims,
the right stick walks and the left one turns, dashes and crouches.
X jumps, Y drops the magazine, A reloads and interacts, B switches weapons,
and the right stick click is the D-pad. Button prompts show these buttons.
Hand aim  (off = Decoupled VR Head Aim)

ON (Hand Aim): the controller points the weapon and VRIK drives the arms.
OFF (Decoupled VR Head Aim): the WEAPON follows your head instead, the game
keeps owning its position and its ADS animations, and VRIK stands down for
the weapon arm. Either way the shot leaves the real muzzle, for guns and
projectiles alike, and free-look while aiming is preserved.
Weapon Aim laser dot (where the bullet hits)

Red dot projected from the actual weapon muzzle direction through the
game camera -- marks exactly where the bullet will fly.

Haptics: every round by weapon class (handgun, rifle, shotgun, sniper),
melee block and parry, bullet block and deflect, reaching a belt element,
pulling a grenade pin. Two-handed grip: both hands; one hand: one.
Open the VR menu with a grip swipe

Hold the right grip and sweep the hand straight down to open or close the VR menu.
Off: only L3 + R3 (both sticks pressed) opens it.
A hand holding something (the steering wheel, a ladder, an item) never opens it.

OR the VR controller state into XInput gamepad 0 every poll.
Off = the game only sees a physical pad / nothing.

ON  - every equipped weapon hangs on the body where it belongs:
      pistols on the right hip, blades and clubs on the left hip,
      rifles and shotguns over the shoulders, knives on the chest.
      Reach for one and squeeze the grip to draw it (a blade at the
      hip is pulled out along its handle); grip at its place to put it away.
OFF - no weapons on the body, fixed slot per zone:
      over-shoulder = EquipmentSlot1, right hip = Slot2, left hip = Slot3.

On: the gun shows the free hand what it needs - an empty magazine pulses,
the place of a removed one stays lit, the bolt or the slide to rack glows.
Off: no highlight; the reload itself works the same.

On: speed follows left-stick travel. Off: the current fixed-speed movement (default).
Vehicle controls keep their existing response.

Raw travel that produces full analog input and activates sprint, dash and crouch.
The usable travel between the deadzone and this threshold maps to 0-100%%.

Game     - left stick walks the way the camera faces (vanilla).
HMD      - left stick walks the way the headset faces.
Left/Right hand - walks the way the chosen controller points.
Vehicles always keep game heading.
Height loss after the measured lean. Standing back up releases physical crouch.

In water: reach forward with both hands, sweep out and pull back.
Movement begins during the pull. Gentle strokes swim normally; fast pulls boost.
Swim where the headset points, including up/down; no stick needed.
To rise, raise separated hands to chest level and push both down.
Repeat strokes to keep moving. Pull the left stick back to stop.

Grip a side rail or rung. Pull the hand down to climb up,
or move it up to climb down. Release to stop. Native pelvis and legs stay on the ladder.

After an upward pull near the top, finish climbing even when grips are released.
Move the stick or push a held hand upward to cancel.

Convert the right-stick X axis into discrete snap pulses
instead of smooth rotation. Helps with motion sickness.
Off can improve GPU utilization and FPS, but may increase input latency.
Limit FPS to the headset refresh rate

Frames above the headset's refresh rate are never shown: they only load the GPU
and make the picture stutter now and then. Off lets the game run free.

One picture for both eyes, drawn once from the centre of the head:
no depth, the most frames. Engine stereo and the second view are off.

Forward-predicts the head pose by this many ms using head
velocity, hiding render-to-photon latency. 0 = off.
Tune up until motion feels responsive without overshoot.

Personal fine-tune on the auto IPD. 1.0 = calibrated natural
separation, auto-scaled to the headset's runtime IPD. Nudge
0.8-1.2 for taste; crank to 3-5x to exaggerate depth and make
the eye alternation obvious on the flat monitor for testing.

Scales eye separation AND head translation together.
Lower it (e.g. 0.8) to make the world look
BIGGER / yourself smaller; raise to shrink the world. Use this if V
and NPCs feel too large.

Eye-separation multiplier on the runtime IPD. 1.0 = the neutral
baseline (+-0.033 m on a typical headset).
Affects stereo depth (diorama vs giant), NOT the monocular size.

On stale ticks, re-submit the last clean captured eye and let
the compositor reproject it, instead of warping stale content
again. May lower submit rate
toward the capture rate. Off = always warp the stale eye.

ON: each eye renders exactly its own off-centre lens window
(more of the panel used, square pixels).
OFF: the symmetric frustum sized to the widest half-angle.
VR shortcuts and default game actions. Button names follow the Touch / Xbox convention; game actions use your controller bindings.
Move. Hold fully forward for 0.2 seconds to sprint.
Rack the weapon / release the slide.
With a weapon: release the magazine. Holstered: Back / close.
Equip or holster the weapon at the reached slot.
Grab the magazine during a reload.
Toggle the scanner. Squeeze again to close it.
Activate cyberware once. Release both to use again.
BOTH HANDS  Reach, sweep out, pull back
Swim in the direction you look. Movement starts during the pull; gentle strokes swim normally and fast strokes boost.
BOTH HANDS  Raise, then push down
Cancel gesture propulsion. Stick movement takes priority.
Page through quickhacks. Partial movement still walks.
Hold LEFT STICK press + RIGHT STICK
Push the right stick fully up, down, left or right to send that D-pad direction.
Confirm a dialogue choice. The normal handbrake action remains available.
Grab the wheel or handlebars with that hand. Release to let go.
VR follows the camera chosen by the game, including third-person scenes. Driving and seated-camera options are in DRIVING.
Open or close the VR menu in front of you (as the right-hand swipe down does).
Move the panel farther away / closer.
Open or close this overlay from the keyboard. ESC closes it.
Change game actions in Settings > Key Bindings > Controller. VR gesture settings are in CONTROLS and AVATAR.
Catch up after 3 seconds at rest when the offset is over 10 degrees inside the cone.
External OFXR is loaded: disarm its tray and restart before native generation
Waiting for matching depth and motion vectors in both eyes
Generating with engine motion vectors and depth
Paused in menus or untracked views
Framegen requires the current SDR RGBA8 capture format
DLSS Frame Generation could not create its features
Backend failed; toggle generation off/on or change the backend
NVIDIA DLSS SDK was not built into this plugin
DLSS Frame Generation needs a newer NVIDIA driver
DLSS Frame Generation is not supported on this GPU (RTX 40/50 required)
Full-body calibration works in game only: load a save first.
Step 1: look ahead at the horizon line, then press both triggers (press to cancel)
Release both triggers, take the pose, then pull both together.
Step 2: arms down, look down, then press both triggers (press to cancel)
Step 3: face the cross: head on its top, arms straight out along its arms, until the countdown ends (press to keep V's arms)
Stand facing the cross; the dots turn green on their marks, then the countdown runs.

V's hips and legs follow your waist and foot trackers (needs a calibration).
The spine, head and arms stay as before.
V's spine and head follow the headset

V's spine bends from your hips to your headset, V's eyes on your view (with the legs on).
The arms stay as before.

V's arms reach your controllers with V's arm length set by the calibration (with the spine on).
Off: the arms as before.
Not taken: look straight at the horizon line until it turns green, then press again
Not taken: stretch both arms straight out along the cross, then hold still again
Not taken: stand straight with the headset, trackers and controllers tracked, then press again

Each of V's fingers follows your own, from hand tracking (finger-tracking gloves, Index controllers).
Off: finger poses from the buttons.
Grip input from finger position instead of the sensor

The grip is a fist or a thumbs-up, from the fingers' position,
not the controller's grip sensor: a relaxed hand never grips.

V's fingers also spread sideways as yours do.
Off: the fingers only bend, from the curl.

V's fingers spread sideways as yours do.
0: off, the fingers only curl. 1: default.
Keep HUD in front of the world

The HUD comes closer when a wall or a person is nearer than Depth.
Off: always at Depth.
0: same size on screen. 1: same size in the world.
Hands push the HUD out of view

While a hand is in front of the HUD, the HUD grows until its elements leave the view,
so your hands are not covered by it.

How far the HUD moves out while a hand is in front of it.
1: not at all. 2: to the edge of the view, a small head turn away. 3: fully out of view.

The prompt sits 10 cm in front of the object it names.
Interaction distance is then used only when nothing is targeted.

Same as right-handed: the buttons and sticks as right-handed; only the triggers
and grips go with the weapon hand.
Left stick walks: the buttons mirrored (X jumps, A reloads...), the sticks as they were.
Left stick turns: the buttons and the sticks mirrored.

Hold the left stick forward: the stick held at the stop for a moment sprints (default).
Click the left stick: a click sprints until the stick is let go.

Hands and arms stop at the body and at each other.
Empty hands also stop at walls and furniture (static world geometry).
Only the drawn arm stops; your real hand does not.

Seated, hands stop at the body and each other, not at the car.
A hand on the wheel is never stopped.

An empty hand clear of the body shoves bottles, crates and the like, and a hand pressed
against a light prop knocks that one prop loose. Never in a vehicle.
Experimental: turn it off if the player is ever thrown about.

Closing an empty hand, each finger stops where it meets something, so a hand
rests on a table or closes round a pipe. Never in a vehicle.

Squeeze the grip at a loose object to carry it, let go to drop or throw it. One hand lifts
about 6 kg, two about 30, and the other hand can take it over.
Experimental: turn it off if the player is ever thrown about.

For finding faults, and it costs frame rate. Stays off after a restart.
Blue the hands, cyan the fingers, magenta people. From PhysX within 2 m: grey the world, yellow what moves.
Rays: green free, red up to what they hit. In a carried thing: orange the place taken, white the palm.
Carried objects stick to the hand

Draws a carried thing on the hand in the same frame, while its body follows in the physics.
Against a wall the picture goes back to the body. Off: the picture is on the body, and trails a swing.

Physics reaches the screen after the hand does. Raise it until a thing swung fast stops trailing the hand,
lower it if it runs ahead when the hand stops.

The game's collision is simpler and often smaller than what is drawn. More distance keeps
hands and fingers out of the mesh, and makes them stop a little before they touch.
Hold a car's wheel anywhere on the rim

Your hand stays where you took hold and slides round the rim with your own hand, so
you can steer one-handed from the top and change grip in a hard turn.
Off: a grab puts the hand where the driving animation holds it. Bikes always do.

Motorcycle handlebars: push one hand forward and pull the other back.
This is how far the bars turn, seen from above, to reach full lock. Lower = more sensitive.
Two hands use the line between them; one hand turns about a point half the bars' width to its side.
Adding or releasing a hand keeps the current turn.

Lean your body sideways to steer a motorcycle, added to your arms while holding the bars.
The value is the share of full lock from a 15 cm lean; 0 turns it off.
Centre is where your body was when you grabbed the bars.

A motorcycle's own seated offset, used instead of the Car Head sliders
while you ride one and ignored everywhere else. Zero = no offset.
(not on a motorcycle: these are ignored)
